svg.title: Hydroxyapatite phase fraction during SBF immersion for ceramics sintered at 700 to 1100 °C
svg.desc: Left: hydroxyapatite weight percent versus immersion time. Right: change relative to day 0.
svg.text: Hydroxyapatite evolution in simulated body fluid
Hydroxyapatite fraction of bioactive silicate ceramics sintered at 700–1100 °C, followed over 21 days of SBF immersion
Sintering temperature sets the starting fraction: 700 °C is the most apatite-rich (37–44 wt%), 800 °C the lowest (7–10 wt%).
700 °C also changes most over time (up to +6.6 wt% at day 14); the other temperatures stay within about ±3.5 wt% of day 0.
HA and fluorapatite overlap at Cu Kα and are not separated by XRD; fractions are relative to the quantified crystalline phases.
